items.stem: What is an ideal contraceptive? Describe natural, barrier, IUD, oral and surgical methods of contraception with one example each.
items.answer: Ideal: user-friendly, available, effective, reversible, no or least side effects, no interference with sexual drive. Natural: periodic abstinence (days 10–17). Barrier: condoms/diaphragms. IUDs: Cu-T (copper), LNG-20 (hormone), Lippes loop (non-medicated). Oral: pills with progestogens/oestrogen, Saheli (weekly, non-steroidal). Surgical: vasectomy, tubectomy.

items.stem:

items.answer: (a) Vasectomy: surgical method in males; small part of vas deferens removed or tied; blocks sperm transport. Copper releasing IUD (Cu-T): inserted into the uterus; releases Cu ions; suppresses sperm motility. (b) Vasectomy.
